ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated List, Spanish AEAT and Guardia Civil lists, and PEP databases such as World-Check or local equivalents

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish language using Latin alphabet; foreign names must be transliterated or translated into Spanish where required by local naming conventions

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, file an administrative appeal before the Registro Mercantil within 30 days; failure to appeal may lead to judicial review or administrative sanctions

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, by which the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act) is approved; applicable formation and capital sections are Articles 20-32 (formation), 58-61 (registered office), 62-65 (share capital), and 100-104 (administration and officer appointment).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the name certificate and Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) for the final registration of the deed, both overseen by the Ministry of Justice (Ministerio de Justicia).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) and its mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL must have a minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 3,000. The capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the Company's name before execution of the deed; the bank's Certificado de Desembolso (capital deposit certificate) must be presented to the notary. The deposited capital cannot be withdrawn until the Company is registered in the Commercial Registry. Non-cash contributions require an independent valuation report under Article 67 LSC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation deed and Bylaws of the Company be approved and that the directors be authorized to execute and file all constitutional instruments. RESOLVED THAT the statutory share capital of EUR 3,000 has been fully subscribed and paid up by the founding members as set forth in the bank certificate. RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Company be fixed at Calle de la Industria 45, Madrid, Spain, within jurisdiction of the Madrid Commercial Registry. RESOLVED THAT the Company's Executive Chair and Secretary be appointed, and that the Managing Director be granted daily authority to open bank accounts, obtain tax registration, engage employees, and complete municipal licensing. All resolutions effective upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Ministry of Justice, Madrid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application at the Registro Mercantil Central portal requesting certification that the proposed corporate name is not registered. Propose one preferred name and two alternatives. The certificate is valid for three months and must be submitted to the notary with the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney of the incorporator (if represented)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or contradicted, resubmit the application within the same procedure choosing another alternative name; no prejudice to the priority of the original petition once corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Minimum Share Capital and Obtain Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish commercial bank registered with the Bank of Spain.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the Company's name, deposit the fully subscribed share capital (minimum EUR 3,000), and request a Certificado de Desembolso (capital deposit certificate). The certificate must identify the depositing shareholders and the deposited amount and be presented to the notary.
required_dossiers: Passports and NIEs of all founding members
Draft incorporation deed with the corporate name certificate
Anti-money-laundering declaration and source of funds forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional compliance declarations under anti-money-laundering rules, provide the standard source-of-funds statements; the deposit remains available for re-designation to the registered company upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarise the Incorporation Deed (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the registered office district in Madrid, attached to the Colegio Notarial de Madrid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter the Spanish notary with the negative name certificate, bank capital certificate, and draft bylaws. The notary authenticates the deed, obtains the provisional NIF (NIF provisional) if requested, and sends a certified copy to the Commercial Registry for registration. Pay the notarial fees and stamp duty (Impuesto sobre Actos Jurídicos Documentados) on the authorized capital.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects defects, execute an Acta de Subsanación (rectification deed) before the same notary; re-signing is instantaneous once the defect is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (Madrid Provincial Commercial Registry).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed (first copy) and Form 600 tax payment certificate within two months of execution with the provincial registry of the registered office. The examiner (Registrador) issues a legal qualification; if approved, issues the registration entry confirming the Company's legal personality.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarised incorporation deed
Certified copy of NIE of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar writes a nota de calificación (qualification note), cure the stated defect by filing a supplementary deed or document; appeal the qualification if the defect is erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF Definitivo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — State Tax Administration Agency.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, submit Form 030 to the AEAT office with the Commercial Registry registration certificate to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF. AEAT will confirm the definitive NIF and issue the corresponding electronic registration certificates needed for invoicing and social security.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Commercial Registry
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to mismatched data, present the corrected registration certificate or amend the deed and file a rectification at the AEAT office; timely correction prevents tax accrual penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Employer with Social Security and Complete Municipal Activity Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and Ayuntamiento de Madrid — Department of Urbanism, Environment and Economic Activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company as an employer with TGSS (Forms TA.6 and TA.7) and file the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) declaration at the municipal office. Apply for the municipal environmental and activity authorization (Licencia de Actividad / Comunicación Ambiental) for the industrial assembly workshop. These filings constitute the open-for-business conditions.
required_dossiers: Proof of workplace fitness (fire safety certificate, occupancy license)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal activity license is omitted, the Company must promptly file a Declaración Responsable and rectify the municipal administrative file; repeated failure may result in a closure order, so immediate correction is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas de la Comunidad de Madrid and Concejalía de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad del Ayuntamiento de Madrid.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Activity License / Declaración Responsable for the assembly and repair of electric cargo bicycles at the industrial workshop; a mandatory statutory sectoral license is not required for this low-impact ISIC 3091 manufacturing activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Agricultura e Interior de la Comunidad de Madrid — Directorate General for Environmental Quality.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA under Ley 21/2013, Annex II; subject only to a simplified environmental communication (Comunicación Ambiental) because the assembly of light electric vehicles is classified as a low-impact activity without significant land, water, or emission-intensive processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to the municipal sewerage system must comply with municipal by-law limits (pH 6-9; suspended solids <300 mg/l; COD <750 mg/l, if any). VOC emission limit for auxiliary painting or coating processes must remain below 50 mg C/m³ under Royal Decree 117/2003 when coatings are applied. Battery waste must be independently managed under Royal Decree 110/2015, requiring a take-back scheme, a repair route, and strict recordkeeping.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire protection certificate (Certificado de Instalación y Mantenimiento de Protección Contra Incendios), building occupancy and structural inspection certificate (ITEO/ITE) issued by a certified architect, and workplace health and safety verification (Plan de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales) notified to the competent labor authority through the applicable mutua.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), through its Sede Electrónica (Electronic Office). Regional tax authorities administer certain taxes in the Basque Country and Navarre; the target jurisdiction is otherwise subject to the common national tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish SL obtains a Spanish NIF through the AEAT. Following incorporation, its representative files Modelo 036 to obtain or confirm the NIF, ordinarily using the incorporation deed and evidence of registration or pending registration with the Commercial Registry. A provisional NIF may be issued during formation; the definitive NIF must be confirmed after registration and completion of the required filings. A foreign legal entity conducting taxable activity in Spain applies for a Spanish NIF using Modelo 036 and supplies formation, registry, identity, and representative documentation, with legalization or translation where required. For VAT transactions requiring an EU VAT number, the entity requests inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) through Modelo 036; the resulting VAT number is validated through VIES. A non-EU taxable person may be required to appoint a Spanish VAT fiscal representative, subject to applicable EU rules and exemptions. Tax registration does not itself establish a permanent establishment or determine corporate tax residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is generally a separate corporate income-tax taxpayer; Spain has no general US-style check-the-box election for an SL. Statutory optional regimes may be available subject to eligibility and election requirements, including tax consolidation and specified special regimes. Hybrid-mismatch rules apply under Spanish law and EU-derived provisions; they do not constitute a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA), within the EU VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold: a taxable person carrying out VAT-taxable activity in mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands generally must register before commencing the activity. The EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies only to specified cross-border intra-EU distance sales and qualifying electronically supplied or other telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronic services under the applicable rules; it is not a general Spanish domestic registration threshold. The Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the EU VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not generally require advance real-time tax-authority clearance of every domestic VAT invoice. The Immediate Supply of Information system (SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including those subject to monthly VAT returns and certain electing taxpayers, to electronically report invoice-record data to the AEAT, generally within four days subject to statutory counting rules and exceptions. The Veri*Factu and electronic invoicing requirements under Law 11/2021 and Law 18/2022 are subject to implementing rules and applicable rollout dates; taxpayers must verify the rules effective for their accounting system and transaction date. B2B electronic invoicing under Law 18/2022 is being implemented progressively and is not a universal clearance or digital-stamping regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the EU VAT territory to a destination outside it may qualify for the Spanish VAT export exemption with entitlement to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory exporter, supply, and documentary conditions are met and the export is properly evidenced. The exemption may also apply to qualifying services directly connected with exports or other specifically listed services. Services are not generally zero-rated merely because the customer is located offshore: place-of-supply rules, customer status, use-and-enjoyment provisions, and any applicable exemption must be assessed. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate exemption conditions and are not exports for this purpose.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the parties, goods, consideration, and applicable VAT treatment
Export customs declaration and evidence of exit from the EU customs territory, ordinarily including the MRN and customs exit confirmation
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or carrier delivery records
Sales order, contract, packing list, and proof linking the goods supplied to the export declaration and transport records
For services, contract, service-delivery evidence, customer identity and business-status evidence, and documentation supporting the applicable place-of-supply or exemption treatment
Inward remittance evidence only where relevant to substantiate payment or commercial records; it is not a universal statutory condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days: No general Spanish statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applies as a condition for export VAT exemption or refund. Payment and reporting obligations, if any, must be assessed separately under applicable financial, sanctions, and transaction-specific rules.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The taxpayer must retain reliable evidence supporting the export exemption and input-tax deduction and produce it during an AEAT audit. If the exemption is unsupported or conditions are not met, the AEAT may assess output VAT, deny or recover input-VAT refunds, charge late-payment interest, and impose penalties under the General Tax Law. Depending on the facts and severity, tax penalties can generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax; separate penalties may apply for accounting, invoicing, or reporting violations. Fraudulent conduct may also trigger criminal liability where statutory thresholds and elements are met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business; the Banco de España is the supervisory authority for credit institutions, payment systems, balance-of-payments statistics and the external-transaction reporting regime, while the DGCIIN administers the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (foreign investment registry). Spain is a Eurozone member, so monetary policy and foreign-reserve management are ultimately vested in the European Central Bank within the Eurosystem, with the Banco de España acting as the national competent authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates a fully liberalised and freely convertible currency regime. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted under Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and under Spanish Law 18/1962 (as amended) on the foreign-exchange banking regime. The euro (EUR) is fully convertible, and there are no surrender requirements, no central-bank prior-approval procedures, no soft-exchange-rate controls and no exchange-rationing rules. Profit remittances by an SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted, but the paying company must satisfy: (i) the distributable-capital safeguards of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, including the mandatory legal reserve of 5% of annual profit until the reserve reaches 20% of share capital, the set-off of prior-year losses and the absence of a net-asset deficit; (ii) the corporate-income-tax (IS) settlement and the correct accounting base; (iii) the non-resident withholding tax applicable to dividends (the WHT is reduced under double-tax-treaty networks and generally 19% for eligible EU/EEA residents, with the standard statutory rate for other non-residents); and (iv) bank-level reporting of the payment under the Banco de España external-transactions statistics and AML/CFT rules. The practical hurdle is not legal convertibility but documentary proportionality: receiving/remitting banks must evidence the economic substance of flows, the underlying commercial or capital instrument, and the tax status of the beneficiary before executing any significant Latin American or Asian corridor payment. Spain maintains no list of blocked currencies and no priority foreign-exchange allocation scheme; capital exports could only be restricted by an exceptional EU-wide safeguard (e.g., financial-sanctions measures related to sanctioned counterparties), none of which applies to this low-risk micro-mobility manufacturing entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion timeline and no required conversion ratio apply in Spain. Exporters may invoice, hold, collect and convert export receipts in any convertible currency; there is no obligation to repatriate export proceeds within a fixed period and no obligation to convert USD, MXN, BRL or CNY collections into EUR. The mandatory disciplines for this ISIC 3091 electric cargo e-bike manufacturer are documentary and statistical: (i) extra-EU exports require a customs export declaration (DUA) lodged in the Spanish Customs electronic system, with the export-VAT exemption (0% VAT) evidenced on the commercial invoice; (ii) intra-EU dispatches to other Member States are monitored through the Intrastat threshold (approximately EUR 400,000 annual dispatch threshold for goods) and must be declared to the Spanish Tax Administration (AEAT); (iii) export collections arriving through the banking system must carry the underlying invoice and transport documents so that the receiving bank can classify the flow in the Banco de España external operations statistics; and (iv) the export prices and proceeds must comply with the transfer-pricing arm's-length principle where the buyer is a related party. The practical operational rule is that all export receipts are credited to the SL's domestic EUR-denominated account, optionally after a spot conversion by the bank at the ECB reference rate; the exporter must simply preserve the customs, invoice, banking and transport evidence for inspection by AEAT, the customs authority and the financial institution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito for the subscribed share capital prior to Notary certification and Registro Mercantil inscription)
Operational current account with international desk, SWIFT multi-currency capabilities and trade-finance platform
Operational current account with integrated FX portal, gpi-correspondent clearing and documentary-credit facilities
Operational EUR account with LatAm correspondent network, LC issuance desk and SME treasury products
Operational current account with trade-collection services and supply-chain finance
Operational current account with flexible treasury and forward-FX execution for medium-sized OEM manufacturers
Operational current account through the regional network for domestic liquidity concentration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions that hold a valid PSD2 passport into Spain; LOW for offshore or non-EU digital EMIs. A Spanish SL may lawfully hold payment accounts with an EU-authorised EMI, but an EMI is not a credit institution, is not supervised by the Banco de España as a bank, cannot grant overdraft or working-capital credit, cannot issue commercial documentary letters of credit or standby guarantees in the manner of a Tier-1 bank, and its deposit-like balances do not benefit from the Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos (Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme); immunity is replaced by the safeguarding/segregation duties of the EMD. Offshore EMIs (e.g., UK post-Brexit, BVI, UAE, Gibraltar-based) are not passportable into Spain without a local licence or authorised agent under the Payment Services Law (RDL 19/2018 transposing PSD2), so their onboarding of a Spanish manufacturing SL is either illegal or operationally crippled by correspondent-bank sanctions screening. For this micro-mobility OEM, which must pay Chinese component suppliers, collect LatAm distributor proceeds, settle Spanish payroll/VAT and ultimately remit dividends, an EMI-only treasury is not viable. The recommended configuration is a Tier-1 Spanish bank as the principal operating account and EBICS-connected gateway, optionally supplemented by one EU-passporting EMI multi-currency wallet for low-value, high-volume supplier float; any non-EU foreign account held by the SL must be disclosed to AEAT on Form 720 before 31 March of the following year, and balances above EUR 50,000 require the annual asset declaration, all of which raises compliance cost.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance is the default statutory requirement for the account-opening of a newly formed Spanish SL, although remote onboarding is available under strict and limited conditions. Law 10/2010 (AML/CFT), together with Banco de España guidance, requires the legal representatives, administrators and identified beneficial owners to undergo verified identification; Spanish Tier-1 banks almost always demand that at least one administrator or the duly empowered legal representative attend a branch appointment in person for the initial KYC interview, especially where the shareholders are non-resident Latin American or Asian persons. Remote video identification is accepted only where the director holds a Spanish DNI/NIE or an EU eIDAS-certified digital ID, where the bank's platform performs biometric liveness detection approved by the regulator, and where the institution's risk appetite permits a paperless journey; in practice, non-resident directors without a Spanish tax ID (NIE) are routed to the physical branch process. The efficient blueprint is to appoint one Spanish-resident or EU-resident administrator, or a commercial proxy (apoderado), to appear once at a Santander, BBVA or CaixaBank primary branch in Madrid or Barcelona; the single physical ceremony should simultaneously open the capital escrow account and the operational account, complete the signature authorisation lists (mancomunada period under the Notary), and present the constitutive deed. This reduces onboarding timelines to approximately 5–10 business days and avoids months of iterative sanction-screening questions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of wealth for subscribed capital and initial working capital injected by non-resident shareholders, especially if the parent or ultimate beneficial owner resides in a LATAM high-risk jurisdiction or an Asian manufacturing corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Escritura de Aumento de Capital or escritura de constitución, registered at the Registro Mercantil with the new capital inscription; UBO registry certificates from the foreign parent jurisdiction; three months of parent bank statements evidencing lawful accumulation of funds from real operating revenues; certified corporate financial statements and tax returns of the parent for the last two years; a signed source-of-wealth declaration aligned with FATCA/CRS classifications; and a board-approved written explanation of the economic purpose (component procurement, inventory build-up and export expansion for electric cargo e-bikes).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency supplier payments to Chinese, Vietnamese or Turkish vendors in round-sum amounts that do not match Incoterms, transport documents or customs entries, creating trade-based money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supplier framework agreements; foreign trade licences or business-registry excerpts of the vendors; per-shipment commercial invoices and packing lists; Bills of Lading, CMRs or air waybills consistent with the payment value and dates; customs export/import declarations (DUAs) for extra-EU movements or Intrastat declarations for intra-EU flows; HS-code evidence (CN 8507 batteries, CN 8711 e-bike chassis and electric-power groups); inventory serial-number traceability records; and an audit-ready statement confirming that each wire corresponds to physical goods in transit and not to transfer-pricing round-trips or commission laundering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LatAm distributor proceeds arriving through PSE/acquirer settlement platforms or via third-country financial intermediaries with fragmented FX conversion trails, particularly Mexican Peso, Chilean Peso, Argentine Peso and Brazilian Real receivables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed distributor agreements with resale and exclusivity clauses; the AEAT-matching export declarations and transport evidence proving physical export of goods; FX conversion confirmations issued by the clearing banks or the licensed broker showing ECB/IberEfx reference rates; reconciliation ledgers mapping the acquirer/payment-provider payout reports to specific bank statement credits; Incoterm-based pricing sheets (FOB/CIF/DAP) for each destination; and a statutory declaration certified by the administrator that no informal money brokers, VASPs or shell payment agents were used for the collection chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: One or more directors, shareholders or beneficial owners being classified as politically exposed persons (PEPs) or persons with a criminal/tax-condemnation record, or the SL's management profile containing a legacy insolvency from another jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual KYC packet for each administrator: valid DNI/NIE/passport, current proof of residential address (utility bill or tax receipt), Certificado de Antecedentes Penales with legalisation/apostille from Spain or the home jurisdiction, a signed PEP-status questionnaire, and a non-PEP/non-sanctions self-certification; explanation letter covering any adverse historical public-record event and its judicial resolution; and the bank's internal elevated-monitoring acceptance form with the compliance officer's approval where PEP status is unavoidable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Divergence between the SL's declared tax census activity (IAE epígrafe / NACE code) and the real transaction mix, e.g., the bank observes dividend remittances, intellectual-property royalty payments or large unrelated-party payments inconsistent with a manufacturing entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AEAT Censo Certificado (Certificado de Censos) updated to NACE 30.91 / IAE epígrafe 316.1/316.2; the Spanish corporate-income-tax (IS) settlement and net-asset position; a board-approved annual treasury plan listing expected imports, payroll, plant-rents, equipment capex, intra-group service fees and dividend distributions; the Junta General minutes authorising any dividend and demonstrating compliance with the legal reserve requirement; and a transaction-specific narrative for each unusual flow, including the underlying commercial contract and the applicable tax form (e.g., Form 216 for dividend withholding, Form 123/124 or IRNR declarations for interest/royalties).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential undisclosed foreign bank accounts or fintech wallets held in offshore EMIs by the Spanish entity or its shareholders, triggering AEAT Form 720 penalties and reputational AML concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Form 720 'Declaración informativa sobre bienes y derechos situados en el extranjero' filed on time with the AEAT presentation receipt; a written group policy that all non-EU and non-bank payment accounts are individually listed and centrally controlled; the SL's treasury manual containing a defined whitelist of approved EMI accounts and maximum balance thresholds; periodic reconciliations signed by the administrator; and an independent compliance attestation confirming that no undisclosed accounts or crypto-assets are used to receive trade proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for inbound equity injections, shareholder loans and pre-export working-capital transfers from non-resident parents: (1) Legal perfection: for equity, execute a notarised Escritura de Aumento de Capital and register it at the Registro Mercantil; for shareholder loans, execute a private or notarised loan agreement with commercial-rate interest and file it with the annual financial statements; (2) Wire routing: the foreign parent sends a SWIFT MT103 through its correspondent bank to the SL's Spanish IBAN, which must carry the full Spanish NIF of the SL in the beneficiary field; the sending bank should use an OECD balance-of-payments purpose code equivalent to 'direct investment, equity injection' (e.g., S301/S302 or Banco de España external-transactions concept code for capital contributions, such as the 'Inversión Directa' category of the external statistics regime); (3) Documentation to the destination bank: certified capital-increase deed, bank-supported UBO declaration, Notary date-stamped inscription proof, and the bank's standard 'Justificación de operaciones con el exterior' declaration; (4) Foreign investment registry: direct foreign investments are declared ex-post to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (through the form T-01/DGCIIN) within 30 days of the operation or at the latest before the annual filing deadline; no prior exchange-control authorisation is required because the foreign-investment-screening rules only apply to a short list of security-sensitive sectors, not to micro-mobility manufacturing; (5) FX conversion: if the injection is in USD, CNY or a LatAm currency, the receiving bank converts at the ECB reference rate with a transparent spread and issues an exchange confirmation used for accounting and the cash-flow reconciliation; (6) Anti-money-laundering verification: the outgoing corresponding bank must show the SL's legal name, full address, NIF and the purpose reference 'Aportación de capital / Fondo de comercio exterior' on the MT103, and all originator/beneficiary fields must be fully populated to survive travel-rule and sanctions screening; any inbound transfer exceeding EUR 10,000 will be reviewed, and the SL must be prepared to deliver the underlying capital documentation within 48 hours.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail matrix for outbound disbursements: (1) EU component suppliers: use SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) in EUR with purpose code 'Payment for goods' — these are instant to T+1, zero-FX and benefit from the single euro payments framework; the SL should configure SCT mandates and EBICS electronic banking for each recurring vendor; (2) Extra-EU supplier payments (China, Vietnam, Turkey, UK): SWIFT MT103 via the bank's correspondent network with global-payment-innovation (gpi) and a unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR); each MT103 must include the supplier's full legal name, address, commercial invoice number, customs DUA reference where available, and the goods description in HS-code form; (3) Large component lots: documentary Letters of Credit under UCP600 (sight or 30–90 days) issued via SWIFT MT700 through Santander, BBVA or CaixaBank, with transport documents, packing lists, commercial invoices, certificates of origin and inspection certificates presented in strict conformity; a standby LC (SBLC) may support an advance-payment contract; (4) LatAm customer collections: payments are received primarily as MT103 credits; for Argentine and Venezuelan buyers with inconvertible local currencies, collection is structured through an NDF-based settlement or a confirming house mechanism, never through informal parallel FX brokers; (5) Profit remittances and dividends: outbound MT103 wires from the SL to foreign shareholders with the concept 'Dividend distribution', supported by the Junta General distribution minutes and the Form 216 withholding settlement; the paying bank requires proof of AEAT acceptance before releasing the remittance; (6) Governance: all outbound wires above EUR 10,000 are executed only after a five-eye check in the treasury platform; the SL maintains a sanctioned-party screening database of all suppliers, freight forwarders, insurers and bank counterparts; and the treasury manual requires that the purpose code, invoice number and underlying contract identifier be present on every payment instruction, ensuring full auditability for AEAT, the Banco de España, the customs authority and any future external auditor.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL, EUR/CNH) executed with a licensed Spanish credit institution or an EU-regulated broker under MiFID II documentation, used to lock conversion rates for commercial settlements with LatAm distributors and Asian component suppliers.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or low-convertibility currencies (EUR/ARS, EUR/VES) since physical delivery of Argentine and Venezuelan Pesos is prohibited or impractical under the respective local central-bank capital controls; the NDF is settled in EUR against an agreed reference rate and must always be evidenced by underlying commercial receivables or payables.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS or FX swaps) between EUR and USD/CNH for matching long-lived, capex-denominated import liabilities and for sculpting the maturity profile of shareholder loans, subject to ISDA/CSA documentation and EMIR clearing-margin obligations where the notional exceeds the clearing threshold.

Vanilla FX Options (European-style calls and puts) for strategic hedging of the seasonal LatAm sales pipeline, purchased from a Tier-1 Spanish bank under the bank's appropriateness assessment; exotic, barrier or digital pay-off structures are rejected by Spanish treasury policy because they impair hedge-accounting clarity.
FX Swaps with rollover (TOM/NEXT swap structures) for managing short-term liquidity mismatches between EUR receipts and USD/CNY supplier payments without changing the net open currency exposure.

Liquidity-backed natural hedging and netting: the SL is permitted to denominate trade-enablement invoices with LatAm distributors in EUR where commercially viable, thereby eliminating the need for local-currency derivatives and reducing the hedge ratio to the residual net exposure; the treasury policy caps derivative-driven hedge ratios at 75% of projected net FX exposure so that all derivative use remains flow-hedging rather than speculative under AEAT and CNMV prudential expectations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Financial Statements Deposit): preparation, shareholders' meeting approval, and filing of the annual accounts, management report and, where applicable, statutory audit opinion with the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Mercantile Registry) of the registered office; announcement published in BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Meeting must be held within six months of the fiscal year end (by June 30 for a January 1 – December 31 year-end); approved accounts must be deposited at the Mercantile Registry within one month after approval, i.e., no later than July 31 for a December 31 fiscal year end, under Articles 365 and 366 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Closure of the company's registry sheet (cierre registral) after a formal warning annotation, blocking registration of successive corporate acts (capital increases, director appointments, share transfers) and preventing issuance of positive registry certificates; administrative fine from EUR 100 to EUR 12,000 under Article 378 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (commonly 0.75‰ of total assets, minimum EUR 100)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto sobre Sociedades — Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Modelo 200) for the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish central tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year close, i.e., by July 25 for a December 31 fiscal year end, pursuant to Article 124 of Ley 27/2014 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); payment accompanying the return is due on the same filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges (recargos) under Article 27 of Ley 58/2003 of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), or 20% (after 12 months, plus late-payment interest) of the self-assessed liability; Article 198 LGT fixed penalties from EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 proportioned to the unreported tax base; aggravated non-filing may trigger administrative collection proceedings, embargo of assets, and tax-lien registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalización Electrónica de Libros — telematic legalization and stamping of statutory corporate and accounting books (Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book, Inventory and Annual Accounts Book) at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Mercantile Registry) via the Registro Mercantil Central telematic legalization portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the four months immediately following the date of approval of the annual accounts (Article 27.3 of the Código de Comercio); alternatively, before placing in service any newly opened statutory book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books lose privileged probative value in commercial disputes and courts may disregard them as evidence; the omission may be treated as a formal defect in the accounts deposit procedure and may expose the company to the Mercantile Registry nominal penalty scale (EUR 100 – EUR 1,000)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit under Article 263 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital and Ley 22/2015 de Auditoría de Cuentas when the SL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at fiscal year close for two consecutive years: (i) total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; (ii) net annual turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; (iii) average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies to parent companies preparing consolidated accounts, to entities qualifying as public-interest entities, and to companies whose shareholders holding at least 5% of share capital request a statutory audit under Article 265 LSC
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Plan General de Contabilidad (Royal Decree 1514/2007, as amended by Royal Decree 1/2021), aligned with EU-endorsed IFRS for valuation and presentation; SMEs (empresas de reducida dimensión) may apply the simplified PGC Pymes (Royal Decree 1515/2007); listed groups must present consolidated financial statements under IFRS-EU; all statutory accounts are expressed in EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose a stand-alone annual UBO confirmation return for SLs. Under Law 10/2010 (as amended by Law 6/2023) and Royal Decree 304/2014, the company must maintain an internal Libro de Titularidad Real identifying all beneficial owners (any natural person ultimately holding or controlling 25% or more of capital or voting rights, or exercising control by other means). The UBO declaration must be filed at the Mercantile Registry upon incorporation and updated in the Registro de Titularidad Real within ten business days of any share transfer or change in control. The annual deposit of accounts (Depósito de Cuentas) incorporates a corporate certification that the beneficial ownership register remains accurate and current; the Registrar may require a fresh UBO declaration whenever a shareholding movement is detected. Non-compliance or false declarations constitute AML infringements punishable under Law 10/2010 with fines from EUR 601 to EUR 600,000 depending on classification as leve, grave, or muy grave; the Mercantile Registry may also suspend registration of corporate acts until the register is rectified
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro Registro de Administradores (Register of Directors)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and Annual Accounts Book)
Libro de Titularidad Real (Beneficial Ownership Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $480 – $1,500 per year (EUR 430 – EUR 1,350) for Spanish registered-office rental, statutory correspondence handling, and gestoría/company-secretarial support; typical market range in Madrid/Barcelona for a low-risk manufacturing SL
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,200 – $7,000 per engagement (EUR 2,900 – EUR 6,300) for a voluntary or compulsory statutory audit of a small-to-mid-size manufacturing SL, depending on turnover volume, inventory complexity, and audit firm tier

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% headline rate with R&D tax credits (deduction of up to 100% of eligible R&D expenses), accelerated depreciation for fixed assets, and SME preferential regime with reduced tax base for qualifying small enterprises

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return via AEAT Electronic Headquarters (Sede Electrónica del AEAT)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days after the end of the tax period (for calendar year, by 25 January of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income before tax deductions and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for resident Spanish entities; non-residents file Modelo 210 for Spanish source income
For non-residents, include Spanish source income subject to 19% WHT or treaty rates

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 100 euros per day (maximum 1,500 euros); additional 0.5% of the tax due per month of delay; criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid to Spanish resident companies; 19% for dividends paid to non-resident companies (reduced by applicable double tax treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form 210 (Declaration of Withholding Tax) and Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to the withholding agent or AEAT; provide beneficial ownership certification and DTA substantiation
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under DTAs (e.g., 0% with EU countries, 5% with US); Interest: 19% statutory, reduced to 0% under many DTAs (e.g., EU Interest and Royalties Directive)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File if annual consolidated revenue exceeds 20 million euros; Master File required if group consolidated revenue exceeds 50 million euros
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain implements Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) pursuant to EU Directive 2018/410, requiring adequate substance for entities engaged in relevant activities such as holding intellectual property, financing, or distribution to avoid artificial tax avoidance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations to AEAT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal offense with fines up to 100% of evaded tax plus imprisonment from 6 months to 4 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution of evaded taxes, fines, and possible disqualification from company management; potential criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain adequate TP documentation or apply arm's length principle in intra-group transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 5% of the adjusted taxable base; potential tax reassessment with interest and penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines and disqualification if negligence or willful misconduct is proven

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL without sufficient local employees, assets, or operations to justify commercial presence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Dissolution of company, back taxation, and fines up to 1 million euros; potential criminal liability under AML or tax avoidance rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fines, imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy or tax evasion, and entry bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct due diligence on beneficial owners or report suspicious transactions in cross-border payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions up to 2 million euros or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties including fines and imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for fines, disqualification, and potential criminal charges
